$doc: Vyomi capability registry — S3. One entry per console feature; level per substrate (nano = shared core, also dev_server/unified ingress; offline = appliance). Proven by tests/conformance/test_capabilities.py — a claim the backend does not honour fails CI.

s3.bucket.encryption.title: Default encryption
limitations: Every PutObject/GetObject/HeadObject/CopyObject/CompleteMultipartUpload response carries x-amz-server-side-encryption (and the KMS key id / bucket-key header when configured) reflecting the bucket's default-encryption setting — AES256 by default, matching S3's own always-on default — but objects are not actually encrypted at rest.

s3.bucket.public-access-block.title: Block public access (bucket settings)
limitations: PutBucketAcl/PutObjectAcl with a public canned ACL (public-read, public-read-write, authenticated-read) is rejected with AccessDenied when BlockPublicAcls is on, and PutBucketPolicy is rejected when the policy is public (Principal "*", Effect Allow) and BlockPublicPolicy is on. Existing grants/policies already stored before the block was enabled are not retroactively revoked, and Vyomi does not authenticate requests, so there is no per-request anonymous-access check.

s3.bucket.policy.title: Bucket policy
limitations: PutBucketPolicy validates the document is well-formed JSON and is rejected (see Block Public Access) when it is public and blocked; otherwise the policy is stored and returned verbatim and is not evaluated for request authorization — Vyomi has no IAM principal/condition evaluator.

s3.bucket.lifecycle.title: Lifecycle rules
limitations: All rule actions are enforced, evaluated lazily on list/get/head rather than by a background scheduler: Date-based rules fire deterministically once the date has passed; Days-based rules (Expiration, NoncurrentVersionExpiration, Transition, AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload) use the real elapsed wall-clock, as in real S3. In a versioned bucket, Expiration inserts a delete marker rather than destroying history. Transition flips the current version's reported storage class (no physical tiering of bytes, matching what GetObject/HeadObject can actually observe in real S3 too).

s3.bucket.cors.title: Cross-origin resource sharing (CORS)
limitations: OPTIONS preflight and the Access-Control-* response headers are enforced on actual GET/HEAD/PUT/DELETE requests whose Origin and method match a configured rule; this is wire-level header emulation of CORS, not a real browser's same-origin/CORS enforcement engine.

s3.bucket.ownership.title: Object Ownership
limitations: BucketOwnerEnforced is enforced: every PutBucketAcl/PutObjectAcl call on the bucket is rejected (InvalidBucketAclWithObjectOwnership), matching real S3's "ACLs disabled" behaviour. BucketOwnerPreferred/ObjectWriter are stored and returned but have no further effect, since Vyomi has no per-request uploader identity to attribute ownership to.

s3.bucket.acl.title: Access control list (ACL)
limitations: Bucket and object ACLs are stored and returned (Get/PutBucketAcl, Get/PutObjectAcl); a canned ACL (private, public-read, public-read-write, authenticated-read) now produces the real grant list GetAcl returns. Writes are rejected under Block Public Access / BucketOwnerEnforced (see those capabilities), but grants are not evaluated for request authorization — Vyomi does not authenticate requests.

s3.bucket.object-lock.title: Object Lock
limitations: Object Lock can only be enabled at bucket creation (as in real S3) — PutObjectLockConfiguration on a bucket created without it returns InvalidBucketState. Legal hold (Put/GetObjectLegalHold) and retention (Put/GetObjectRetention, GOVERNANCE/COMPLIANCE) are enforced: DeleteObject for a held/retained version id is rejected, GOVERNANCE can be overridden with x-amz-bypass-governance-retention, COMPLIANCE cannot. A bucket-level DefaultRetention rule (Mode + Days/Years) is now stored and stamped onto every new object version (PutObject/CopyObject/CompleteMultipartUpload) that doesn't carry its own explicit x-amz-object-lock-* headers.

s3.bucket.website.title: Static website hosting
limitations: GET/HEAD are REALLY served over the bucket's own website origin (the relay/dev_server's unsigned /__s3_website__/<bucket>/<key> path, standing in for the real bucket-name.s3-website-<region>.amazonaws.com host): the configured IndexDocument resolves for '/' and any key ending in '/', the ErrorDocument's actual content is served with a 404 status for a missing key, RedirectAllRequestsTo issues a real redirect, and RoutingRules (KeyPrefixEquals, optionally HttpErrorCodeReturnedEquals) rewrite the key (ReplaceKeyWith/ReplaceKeyPrefixWith) and redirect for real. Vyomi has no per-request identity model (same documented gap as s3.bucket.public-access-block), so this never checks whether the object/bucket is actually publicly readable — it serves whatever the bucket's current content is regardless of ACL/policy/Block-Public-Access.

s3.bucket.logging.title: Server access logging
limitations: Server access logging is enforced: once PutBucketLogging names a target bucket, every GET/PUT/HEAD/DELETE/CopyObject on the source bucket writes a real log-line object (bucket, timestamp, operation, key, status, bytes) into the target bucket under TargetPrefix. The one divergence from real S3: delivery is immediate and per-request in this simulator, not the batched/delayed delivery (every few minutes, pooled into one object per window) real S3's internal logging pipeline uses.

s3.bucket.notification.title: Event notifications
limitations: Events (ObjectCreated, ObjectRemoved, DeleteMarkerCreated, TestEvent) are delivered to the configured SQS queues, SNS topics and Lambda functions in this simulator on both substrates — Nano/dev_server delivers through the same in-context SQS/SNS/Lambda stores the native wire itself reaches; the offline appliance delivers through its own appliance-wide stores. EventBridge delivery and delivery retries/DLQ on failure are not modeled.

s3.bucket.replication.title: Replication rules
limitations: PutBucketReplication requires source-bucket Versioning Enabled (as real S3 does). Enabled rules are enforced SYNCHRONOUSLY on PutObject/CopyObject/CompleteMultipartUpload — a matching key is copied into its destination bucket immediately (no async replication-time delay), and the source version's GetObject/HeadObject response carries x-amz-replication-status: COMPLETED. A rule with DeleteMarkerReplication Enabled also propagates a plain DeleteObject's delete marker to the destination. Only destination buckets that exist in this same Vyomi appliance are reachable — real cross-account/cross-region destinations outside it are not. RTC/metrics and replica-modification-sync (bi-directional metadata sync) are not yet enforced.

s3.bucket.accelerate.title: Transfer acceleration
limitations: Transfer acceleration only changes the network path (ingest via a CloudFront edge location) to the same S3 API — there is no behavioural difference for a client to observe, so there is nothing for a single-endpoint simulator to enforce or differentiate.

s3.bucket.request-payment.title: Requester pays
limitations: Requester Pays changes who is BILLED for data transfer and requests; Vyomi has no billing system, so it cannot attribute cost to a payer. What IS enforced is the one wire-visible contract a client actually observes: once Payer is Requester, GetObject/HeadObject reject a request that omits x-amz-request-payer:requester (403 AccessDenied) and echo x-amz-request-charged:requester on one that includes it, exactly like real S3. PutObject/ListObjects are not gated.

s3.bucket.intelligent-tiering.title: Intelligent-Tiering Archive configurations
limitations: Archive-tier transitions are enforced for objects explicitly uploaded with StorageClass INTELLIGENT_TIERING, evaluated lazily on HeadObject/GetObject like lifecycle Transition: once the elapsed real wall-clock time since the object's last-modified date passes a Tiering's Days threshold, matching Filter prefix, HeadObject/GetObject report it via x-amz-archive-status (ARCHIVE_ACCESS / DEEP_ARCHIVE_ACCESS) — the deepest tier whose threshold has fired. The automatic, config-free Frequent<->Infrequent-Access tiering every object gets after 30 days with no reads is not modeled (Vyomi doesn't track per-object read recency), and an archived object's bytes stay retrievable without a RestoreObject call (no restore-request/temporary-copy lifecycle).

s3.bucket.inventory.title: Inventory configurations
limitations: A real manifest.json + manifest.checksum + CSV data file, listing the source bucket's ACTUAL objects (sizes, ETags, storage classes, every version when IncludedObjectVersions=All), is written into the destination bucket — lazily evaluated (no background scheduler): the first access generates it immediately, later ones regenerate only once the configuration's real Schedule.Frequency (Daily/Weekly) has actually elapsed. Only Format=CSV produces a data file; ORC/Parquet configurations are accepted and stored but Vyomi has no ORC/Parquet encoder, so no data file is written for them (the manifest still lists the real object count, with a note in fileFormat). Only a destination bucket that exists in this same appliance is reachable.

s3.bucket.metrics.title: Metrics
limitations: Every PutObject/GetObject/HeadObject/DeleteObject/ListObjects(V2) request that matches a configured filter's prefix publishes real AWS/S3 CloudWatch datapoints AS IT HAPPENS — AllRequests, GetRequests/PutRequests/HeadRequests/DeleteRequests/ListRequests, 4xxErrors, BytesDownloaded, BytesUploaded, dimensioned by BucketName + FilterId — derived from actual request activity, never synthetic. There is no recurring publish schedule (real CloudWatch batches on ~1-minute boundaries; here a point lands the instant the request is served) and PostRequests/5xxErrors/FirstByteLatency/TotalRequestLatency/storage metrics (BucketSizeBytes, NumberOfObjects) are not yet produced.
